extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the HHMI Investigator Program (biomedical researchers at eligible U.S. institutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/selection criteria for applying to the HHMI Investigator Program: who may apply, what materials to submit, and the qualities HHMI looks for in selecting Investigators. Intended for biomedical researchers seeking HHMI Investigator appointments at eligible U.S. institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection focus — people, not projects
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI supports people, rather than projects, because it’s individual scientists who break barriers to advance knowledge. HHMI selects people, not projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on the individual applicant's track record, creativity, independence, and potential to catalyze discovery rather than on a single proposed project. Look for evidence that the candidate pursues fundamental questions, takes intellectual risks, and drives research programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence, discovery, and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators ... are widely known for their scientific discoveries, their innovation, and their success in pushing the bounds of knowledge in biomedical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI seeks researchers with demonstrated high-impact discoveries and a history of innovation — e.g., developing new tools and methods or opening new lines of investigation. Evidence can include landmark papers, influential methods, or breakthroughs that changed understanding in a field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to ask tough questions and accept risk of failure
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Investigators ask tough questions in science, even at the risk of failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors candidates who pursue bold, high-risk/high-reward science rather than only conservative, guaranteed-success projects. Demonstrate examples where you pursued challenging problems or approaches that faced significant uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool and method development
rubrics_metrics.description: They develop new tools and methods that make it possible to ask previously unapproachable questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight creation of experimental/analytical tools, technologies, or methodologies that enable new science. Novel methods that broaden the ability of the field to address problems are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary linkage to biology and medicine
rubrics_metrics.description: Many forge links between biology and medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how your work connects basic biological insight to medical relevance or integrates across disciplines to open new avenues of biomedical research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to mentoring and training
rubrics_metrics.description: They are committed to mentoring and training the next generation of scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of mentorship, training outcomes (trainees' careers, publications, grants), and plans for fostering the next generation in your lab and institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree requirement (PhD/MD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a PhD and/or MD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit eligibility requirement; applicants without one of these degrees are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research location eligibility — U.S. institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must plan to perform research at one of over 200 eligible U.S. institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that your host institution is on the list of eligible institutions (see 'Eligible Institutions' download/link). The appointment is tied to performing research at an eligible U.S. institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional commitment / position requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a position that represents substantial commitment by their institution, such as a tenure-track faculty position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your position should demonstrate institutional support (e.g., tenure-track or equivalent) and willingness of the host institution to enter the collaborative agreement required for an HHMI Investigator appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record of peer-reviewed funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have a track record of peer-reviewed funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documentation of prior peer-reviewed grants or equivalent competitive funding as evidence of sustained support and review by peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required length of post-training professional experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Each competition defines a required length of post-training, professional experience prior to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility with respect to career stage varies by competition; check the specific Program Announcement for the competition you intend to enter for the exact required post-training experience window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary breadth — scope of eligible fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Each competition defines the breadth of scientific disciplines to be considered; however, most competitions are open to most biological and biomedical disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm whether your discipline is in scope for the specific competition via the Program Announcement; most biological/biomedical areas are typically eligible but specific competitions may narrow scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials — five highlighted research articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Application requirements include five highlighted research articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and submit five publications that best represent your scientific contributions. These are core elements reviewers use to assess impact and leadership in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials — summary of major research contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Application requirements include a summary of your major research contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise narrative summarizing your most important scientific contributions and their significance, situating the five highlighted articles and other accomplishments in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials — program description (ongoing and planned research)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application requirements include a program description focused on your ongoing and planned research program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe your current research agenda and planned future program, emphasizing direction, novelty, feasibility, and how HHMI support would enable transformative progress. HHMI funds people and labs broadly, so frame the narrative at the program level rather than a single short-term project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process — direct application (no nomination) and institutional limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants apply directly; there is no nomination process and no limit on the number of applications from a single institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates submit their own applications; institutions do not need to nominate and may have multiple applicants in a competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process — review by HHMI leadership and panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of investigators is made by HHMI scientific leadership and is based on assessment by a panel of distinguished scientists, including members of HHMI advisory boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that external panels of distinguished scientists assess applications; selection decisions are then made by HHMI scientific leadership. Emphasize elements that expert peers will evaluate (impact, originality, programmatic vision, mentorship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment terms and renewal criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The HHMI investigator appointment has a seven-year renewable term. Renewal decisions are made by HHMI scientific leadership, based on assessment by a panel of distinguished scientists, including members of HHMI advisory boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that appointments are time-limited (7 years) and renewal is competitive, requiring demonstration of continued excellence and productivity to an external panel and HHMI leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators as HHMI employees and funding/support provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are employees of HHMI and receive salary and benefits from the Institute. Investigators are provided generous financial support for research as well as access to capital equipment funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should understand employment and funding model (salary/benefits from HHMI plus research support). This affects institutional arrangements and the collaborative agreement with the host institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for institutional engagement and community participation
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to their research programs, HHMI Investigators participate in educational activities and hold leadership roles at these host institutions. Investigators belong to a community of nearly 300 investigators ... They annually attend one of several scientific meetings that highlight science within the Institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be prepared to engage in mentoring, educational activities, leadership roles at their host institution, and participate in HHMI community events and meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition timing and procedural details
rubrics_metrics.description: Through periodic competitions, HHMI invites applications from eligible scientists. Subscribe to HHMI News to receive updates on future competitions. (Dates listed for 2020–2022 cycle were shown on the page.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Program Announcement and HHMI News for exact deadlines, timeline milestones (semifinalists, symposia, finalists, appointment start), and downloadable resources (Program Announcement, Eligible Institutions, FAQs).
